title: I’m building a voxel colony game solo, with AI helping across almost every part of development
author: Arrock12
selftext:
Hey! I’m solo developing StoneEra, a voxel colony survival and management game.

You start with a small group of settlers and build a colony from the ground up. There’s procedural world generation, building, farming, mining, crafting, NPC jobs and priorities, animals, caves, seasons, rivers and other systems that all interact with each other.

The video here shows one of the systems I’ve been working on recently — dynamic water.

Water flows through the voxel terrain, so you can dig channels, redirect rivers, build dams, and use pumps and pipes to move water around. Farms need water, pumps have limited range and height, and lakes can actually be drained.

One of the interesting parts of making StoneEra has been seeing how much AI can help a solo developer beyond just writing code.

I use it while working on gameplay systems and debugging, but also heavily on the asset side. It helps me prototype ideas for voxel models, figure out how buildings, machines or other objects should look, create references, and iterate on designs before I spend time actually building them.

I also use AI while working with animations, UI ideas, textures and visual concepts.

Audio is another big one. I’ve been experimenting with AI for music, ambient sounds and other audio so I can create and test the atmosphere I want without having a separate composer or sound designer for every little thing.

And then there are all the smaller things around actually shipping a game — writing, translations, Steam content, trailers, marketing material, brainstorming mechanics, balancing ideas, research, etc.

So for me AI isn't really one tool that generates one part of the game. It’s more like an extra pair of hands across the whole development process.

I still build, integrate, test and make the final decisions myself, but it lets me move much faster and attempt systems that would otherwise be pretty difficult to handle alone.

I’m currently preparing StoneEra’s demo for Steam Next Fest in October.

Curious how other solo devs here are using AI outside of coding.

comments.body: can you talk a little about how you are creating assets and doing animation ?

replies.author: Arrock12
replies.body:
I create my game assets in Blender using a reference-based workflow. It usually starts with a basic idea or concept of what I want to build. From there, I generate visual references of the object from multiple angles—front, side, back, and sometimes top or perspective views. I use these images to better understand the shape, proportions, materials, and small details of the asset.  
Once the references are ready, I bring them into Blender and use them as a guide while modeling. I assemble and adjust the geometry, refine the proportions, add the necessary details and materials, and optimize the final model so it fits naturally into the visual style of my game.
